Welcome! This page collects everything from the workshop: the slides, the take-home notebooks, and the reading list. Nothing here requires an R installation — you can read all materials right in your browser and set up R whenever you like.

The [bmm](https://cran.r-project.org/package=bmm) (Bayesian Measurement Models) R package lets you fit cognitive measurement models — signal detection, working-memory measurement, drift diffusion — with a model-first interface: you specify the cognitive model, bmm handles the translation to Bayesian hierarchical estimation in Stan.

### Then: [using bmm on your own data](examples/00_your_own_data.html)

The three segments demonstrate models on datasets that were prepared in advance. This notebook is the bridge to yours: which bmm model fits your paradigm (there are more than the three shown today), what shape your data has to be in, how to write the formula for *your* design, how to set up the Stan toolchain you did not need during the workshop — and what the first few error messages mean when you hit them.

## Run the materials yourself (optional)

1. Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) (≥ 4.3) and [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/).
2. Download the workshop repository: <https://github.com/GidonFrischkorn/ShortWS_CognitiveModelling_bmm>
3. Open `ShortWS_CognitiveModelling_bmm.Rproj`, then run `source("Install_Packages.R")` once and `source("Check_Setup.R")` to verify everything works.

Every model shown in the workshop ships pre-fitted in `models/`, so **you do not need the Stan toolchain** — the notebooks load cached fits and run in seconds.
